correctness.rationale: Each canonical chain-graph class is a false-twin class, so any identifying code omits at most one vertex per class. With every class of size at least two, every class still supplies a selected witness. The nested bipartite adjacency then separates distinct same-side levels and all cross-side pairs, except that for \(p=1\) the two selected singleton traces arising from one omission on each side collide exactly in \(K_{2,2}\). Thus the all-but-one condition is sufficient outside that exception. The product polynomial and minimum-code count are immediate classwise. A fresh independent brute replay on one- and two-level profiles with class sizes two and three matched the theorem.
residual_risks: Singleton canonical classes are excluded; the theorem does not classify arbitrary chain graphs.
